cards.front: Recall a key point about Rehearsal Techniques and Strategies
cards.back: Hot-seating: one person sits in character and answers questions from others — reveals backstory, motivation and relationships.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Rehearsal Techniques and Strategies
cards.back: Role on the wall: drawing an outline of a character and filling it with what they think, feel, experience — builds complex character understanding.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Rehearsal Techniques and Strategies
cards.back: Thought tracking: tapping a performer in a freeze-frame to speak their character's inner thoughts — reveals subtext and hidden feelings.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Rehearsal Techniques and Strategies
cards.back: Conscience alley: two lines of people voice opposing advice as a character walks between them — explores moral dilemmas.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Rehearsal Techniques and Strategies
cards.back: Marking the moment: identifying the most significant moment in a scene and finding a way to highlight it (slow motion, freeze, repetition).

cards.front: What should you know about drama exam tips?
cards.back: When writing about rehearsal techniques in your portfolio, use this structure: What we did (name the technique) → Why we did it (what we wanted to discover) → What we found (what it revealed) → How it improved the piece (the outcome). This shows AO4 evaluation skills.

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: Rehearsal techniques are just warm-up games — they don't really affect the final performance. Correct: Rehearsal techniques are essential development tools. Hot-seating reveals character depths that transform performance choices; thought tracking finds subtext that shapes delivery; conscience alley explores dilemmas that drive the drama. Describe three rehearsal techniques you used during your devising process. Explain why you chose each one and how it improved your final piece.

Rehearsal techniques are central to the devising portfolio (AO4: 30%). You must demonstrate that you used specific techniques deliberately, not randomly. The portfolio must show a clear link between technique, discovery and performance outcome. Without this evidence, marks are limited.
